intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 (CLCRP2) is caused by compound heterozygous mutation in the SEC24D gene on chromosome 4q26.

checks.claim: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 (CLCRP2) is caused by compound heterozygous mutation in the SEC24D gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Three individuals from two families affected by a similar skeletal phenotype were each compound heterozygous for two of these mutant alleles
checks.explanation: The abstract says the compound heterozygous SEC24D mutations cause the phenotype, and that the boy's phenotype most closely resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome.

checks.claim: The SEC24D gene is located on chromosome 4q26.
checks.evidence_quote: we report three mutant alleles in SEC24D, a gene encoding a component of the COPII complex
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature that restates the gene the paper names.

paragraphs.text: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 is an autosomal recessive disorder that resembles osteogenesis imperfecta. Its main features are bone fragility with multiple fractures, craniofacial malformations, and severely impaired ossification of the skull with large, open fontanels.

checks.claim: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: We discovered two novel compound SEC24D mutations of autosomal recessive OI patients.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the SEC24D-related disorder as autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 resembles osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: two fetuses initially suspected to have a severe type of osteogenesis imperfecta
checks.explanation: The title also calls the disorder a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta.

checks.claim: The main features of Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 include bone fragility with multiple fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: All three displayed a severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures with prenatal onset.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that all three affected individuals had multiple fractures.

checks.claim: The main features of Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 include craniofacial malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: The 7-year-old boy had short stature and craniofacial malformations including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, frontal bossing, and down-slanting palpebral fissures.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists the boy's craniofacial malformations.

checks.claim: The main features of Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 include severely impaired ossification of the skull with large, open fontanels.
checks.evidence_quote: All three displayed a severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures with prenatal onset.
checks.explanation: The skull ossification defect is stated, but the abstract does not mention large, open fontanels.

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) described a boy of German origin whose features resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome. He had craniofacial malformations, a large skull ossification defect with open fontanels, and multiple fractures, consistent with a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta.

checks.claim: Garbes et al. (2015) described a boy of German origin whose features resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: a 7-year-old boy with a phenotype most closely resembling Cole-Carpenter syndrome
checks.explanation: The abstract supports a boy resembling Cole-Carpenter syndrome but does not say he was of German origin.

checks.claim: The German boy described by Garbes et al. (2015) had craniofacial malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: The 7-year-old boy had short stature and craniofacial malformations including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, frontal bossing, and down-slanting palpebral fissures.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the boy had craniofacial malformations.

checks.claim: The German boy described by Garbes et al. (2015) had a large skull ossification defect with open fontanels.
checks.evidence_quote: All three displayed a severely disturbed ossification of the skull
checks.explanation: The skull ossification defect is stated, but open fontanels are not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: The German boy described by Garbes et al. (2015) had multiple fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: All three displayed a severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures with prenatal onset.
checks.explanation: The boy is one of the three individuals described as having multiple fractures.

checks.claim: The features of the German boy described by Garbes et al. (2015) were consistent with a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in SEC24D, encoding a component of the COPII machinery, cause a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.explanation: The title describes the disorder as a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta.

paragraphs.text: The compound heterozygous mutations reported by Garbes et al. (2015) indicate that CLCRP2 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

checks.claim: The compound heterozygous SEC24D mutations reported by Garbes et al. (2015) indicate that CLCRP2 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Three individuals from two families affected by a similar skeletal phenotype were each compound heterozygous for two of these mutant alleles
checks.explanation: The compound heterozygous mutations are reported, but the abstract does not explicitly conclude autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Cole-Carpenter syndrome is genetically heterogeneous. Cole-Carpenter syndrome-1 is caused by heterozygous mutation in the P4HB gene.

checks.claim: Cole-Carpenter syndrome is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss genetic heterogeneity of Cole-Carpenter syndrome.

checks.claim: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-1 is caused by heterozygous mutation in the P4HB gene.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The abstract does not mention P4HB.

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) performed exome sequencing on the German boy with a Cole-Carpenter-like phenotype and found compound heterozygous mutations in the SEC24D gene. SEC24D encodes a component of the COPII machinery, which carries cargo from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi. Patient fibroblasts showed procollagen retained in the endoplasmic reticulum, which was dilated, so procollagen secretion was impaired. Garbes et al. (2015) also reported SEC24D mutations in a further family with a similar osteogenesis imperfecta-like phenotype.

checks.claim: Garbes et al. (2015) performed exome sequencing on the German boy with a Cole-Carpenter-like phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: As a result of a whole-exome sequencing study, we report three mutant alleles in SEC24D
checks.explanation: Exome sequencing is stated; the boy's German origin is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: Garbes et al. (2015) found compound heterozygous mutations in the SEC24D gene in the German boy with a Cole-Carpenter-like phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Three individuals from two families affected by a similar skeletal phenotype were each compound heterozygous for two of these mutant alleles
checks.explanation: The boy is one of the three compound heterozygous individuals.

checks.claim: SEC24D encodes a component of the COPII machinery.
checks.evidence_quote: SEC24D, a gene encoding a component of the COPII complex involved in protein export from the ER
checks.explanation: The abstract states that SEC24D encodes a COPII component.

checks.claim: The COPII machinery carries cargo from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi.
checks.evidence_quote: a component of the COPII complex involved in protein export from the ER
checks.explanation: Export from the ER is stated, but the Golgi as the destination is not mentioned.

checks.claim: Fibroblasts from the German boy with SEC24D mutations showed procollagen retained in the endoplasmic reticulum.
checks.evidence_quote: Electron and immunofluorescence microscopy of skin fibroblasts of this individual revealed that ER export of procollagen was inefficient and that ER tubules were dilated
checks.explanation: Inefficient ER export of procollagen means it was retained in the ER.

checks.claim: The endoplasmic reticulum in fibroblasts from the German boy with SEC24D mutations was dilated.
checks.evidence_quote: ER tubules were dilated
checks.explanation: The abstract states the ER tubules in the boy's fibroblasts were dilated.

checks.claim: Procollagen secretion was impaired in fibroblasts from the German boy with SEC24D mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: skin fibroblasts of this individual revealed that ER export of procollagen was inefficient
checks.explanation: Inefficient ER export of procollagen supports impaired secretion.

checks.claim: Garbes et al. (2015) reported SEC24D mutations in a further family with a similar osteogenesis imperfecta-like phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Three individuals from two families affected by a similar skeletal phenotype
checks.explanation: The second family had two fetuses suspected to have severe osteogenesis imperfecta.

paragraphs.text: Sarmah et al. (2010) found that the zebrafish 'bulldog' mutant, which has craniofacial cartilage defects, is caused by mutation in sec24d. In this mutant, chondrocytes fail to secrete collagen, which is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum.

checks.claim: Sarmah et al. (2010) found that the zebrafish 'bulldog' mutant is caused by mutation in sec24d.
checks.evidence_quote: the phenotypes described for the Sec24d-deficient fish mutants vbi (medaka) and bulldog (zebrafish)
checks.explanation: This paper only mentions that bulldog is Sec24d-deficient; the original finding is attributed to Sarmah et al., which this paper does not cite in the abstract.

checks.claim: The zebrafish 'bulldog' mutant has craniofacial cartilage defects.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The abstract does not describe the bulldog mutant's craniofacial cartilage defects.

checks.claim: In the zebrafish 'bulldog' sec24d mutant, chondrocytes fail to secrete collagen.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The abstract does not describe chondrocyte collagen secretion in bulldog.

checks.claim: In the zebrafish 'bulldog' sec24d mutant, collagen is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum of chondrocytes.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The abstract does not describe ER retention of collagen in bulldog chondrocytes.
